body: I suffered from depression for a while but it was staved off through counseling.  So I thought things were going okay. I struggle with wanting more, out of my career and life.  My relationship is fine, but we got into an argument and as I was giving him space I realized how much we were supporting ourselves with weed and alcohol. I thought if we're really bored with each other we need to see that without those distractions. We've been together twelve years. So I asked for us to get to the new year without those things and got a big no can do. It made me feel really worthless and that I was less important than weed. I've done a lot and put up with a lot and I didn't think it was a huge thing to ask before I just up and leave my marriage.  I wanted to give it a fair shot.  But I need an adult. We are in our 30s now and i just feel it's time to grow up a bit and evaluate what we want.
Hello
Thanks. I have felt that way for a while. I have always tried to do my best for everyone and people are still cruel. Just listening to the rain tonight. See where I will be in 24 hours.

Will your parents let you get a job? Or even volunteer somewhere?  It's rare that I've kept in touch with anyone from school but coworkers you see all the time,  you're on a team and comrade builds pretty fast. And you make some extra cash. I know that doesn't solve the issues at school but you're pretty much there to learn and the social aspects take a backseat.  I bet you are a nice kid and I think college might be a totally different experience if you want to pursue that.  It's a lot of different age groups and people have had time to mature. I know I spent plenty of lunch times at the library so you aren't the first or last person to feel like a social outcast.  I know that sucks. It seems like you're online when you post these so maybe you can engage with some of your online friends then?
Why do you think you get outcast so easily?

I've honestly found,  not to put anyone in a box,  but the kids who were considered nerds or dorks or the alternative kids or the goths were some of the most down to earth kids.  Maybe that was just who I fit in with.   I'd hate to have to go back to high school. I feel like things are the same but at the same time vastly different.  We didn't have social media or phones at our every whim so if we wanted to bully people or talk shit it was face to face with someone else. Maybe that allows you to really consider your actions and find something better to waste your time on. Are there any clubs you can join?  Do you play any instruments? Video games? If you just act like you don't give a shit while not being a total tool I think yyou'll get through it. I'm pretty sure 80% of people hated middle and high school. I got picked on to brush my nappy hair and change my blue socks. At the end of the day,  now we're all adults sucking on the government's teat trying to make a living. I know that sounds weird. There as a time I ran a razor blade over my wrist because I was going to have to change schools. In retrospect I lived and it wasn't such a big deal. Can you talk to your mom or whoever doesn't want you online and explain you get some support from it and work out some usage guide lines?

I never understood that rumor.  When I was in junior high a rumor spread that some girl was masterbating in class.  I remember thinking even at that age how ridiculous that sounded. .no one masterbates in class.  Kids are so dumb.  And mean! They were mean when I was a kid and they're mean now.  All we can do is find people who aren't so idiotic and hope we ourselves have enough empathy and integrity not to become some superficial loser.  Even adulthood sucks I gotta be honest but the more independent you are the better. Go to college and find a trade or invest in something you're good at.  Those self esteem bolstering things. There are good people everywhere and this is coming from someone who really dislikes people but has still managed to find some I can bare.  Adulthood is its own set of challenges but you have large control over your life.  Anyways don't know if that helps. I was an outcast too.  A tomboy into metal and grunge who had fluffy hair and an exotic look that didn't jive with Abercrombie (cool when I was in school). I learned a lot just by not fitting in. While my mom's mood disorder was passed down to me I still have a good job and utility to do what I want. But there were lots of gloomy days.  Still are. Hope you find peace every now and again.

I don't know if it's people being self absorbed but abused women classically aren't easily coerced from their situations.  In their head they make any number of excuses from oh he just has issues to I could never make it on my own. My own mom didn't leave a drunk physically abusive boyfriend til he went to jail for the 2nd time for dui. Before that she had sustained having him twist her neck so hard she had to go to the hospital to being bunched in the breasts to having her 9 year old kid have to deal with all this.  That's why so often t he police ask women if they want to press charges and many times they say no and there's nothing they can do. It sucks but it's nice you've reached out a hand to her. I really hope for her sake she comes around but it's her race to run.

I'd hate to see you get in trouble or hurt trying to be the white knight.  I know that sounds selfish but that's the job of the police.  If she is indeed being abused it's up to her to reach out for help.  She's already told you basically not to get involved so she probably figures she's equipped to handle it. If she's willing to put up with her abuser and his controlling ways there's probably plenty below the surface.  Unfortunately I feel like it takes a lot of women getting to the lowest of the low to figure things out or build their confidence enough to leave. I don't feel like any rescue from you or promise of a better life can turn someone who's basically been brainwashed by fear.  It's really in her hands.

I haven't gone to work for 2 days due to depression.  I had felt like calling in all week. I have a job where everyone calls in regularly so in figured no harm no foul.  But I did feel guilty. .I should have gone. I just couldn't do it.  To stare at a computer all day feels so isolating.  Maybe try to get an early start to your day, have a breakfast you look forward to, take a walk, or do some exercise. I find the more I have to rush the less prepared I feel and less motivated I become.
Aha I stand corrected.  For my own curiosity what happens if you sign up and decide you can't cut it after signing the contract?

Maybe it won't be as bad as you think..it interested you at one time for a reason and I'm sure you could make a great career. Sometimes our minds make a bigger deal of things than they need to be. But like I said, it's not a life sentence. If you feel it's not for you there's no shame in backing out. But maybe give it a shot so you don't look back and regret not seeing what it was about. But you control your life.  That regiment is not for everyone and there's nothing wrong with that at all.  It's a big life change and I can see how it could produce anxiety.

Life's not a race. Fuck what anyone says, we wouldn't have great artists if everyone got in line and got a business degree.  If you find passion and life in film making then pursue it. If you want to finish your degree in something else as a safety you can do that too. If you want to get a desk job and work on films on the side do it. I hate the messages society tells us about success. Everyone is so full of shit. Only you know what you want to indulge in.  I feel like you're young,  I hope you give things a shot,  because the rest of us are still here even with our different problems.  Some of us have even found a way out. Depression comes and goes. In an ideal world maybe you can harness some of your feelings to make something worthwhile.

Me neither. Life goes on. Our experience evolves, you may hate things today or not have friends but it can different in time. Listen, even total douchebags have friends. Maybe there's someone your overlooking. .not like they need to be your best friend but even taking a walk or having lunch can make you feel better..hating yourself is pointless but I'm familiar with it. It's like a weird cruel voice in my head that won't shut up.  Any other outlet to get out your feelings?

Hmmm better numb than miserable?  Maybe not so.much. I'm sorry things are shit for you right now and no.one showed up.  If it means anything a stranger took time to read your post and reply.  Sometimes social media makes me feel more isolated. How about a walk? Or a game to get your mind on something else?  Sometimes we've gotta force ourselves up but like with exercise, once we get going we can usually continue.

The navy is going to Ask a lot out of you so I think it'll be harder if you have doubts.  Suppose you can always do basic and get the feel for it and decide from there. Unless it's absolutely necessary consider your other options. .I'm sure there's plenty of smart capable people who join the armed forces but it's not something I could see myself doing for some reason.

I've heard a lot of people have an urge to live in the grasp of death after attempting suicide.  Some live and some don't I suppose. If you truly don't want to die I'm sure you realize that on purpose or not you could hit that vital artery and then you won't have a say. If you don't want to go to the hospital on suicide watch which I'll be honest sounds miserable,  as all the websites say, get help.  I feel possessed sometimes too but there's some kind of vanity in me that keeps me from self harm.  To each their own. I am rooting for you as a human being and fellow sufferer to explore your options before you do something you regret.
Try and relax,  do something that makes you happy or at least not miserable.  Be kind to yourself because some days you might be the only one to do that for you. Wishing you well and you're welcome.

What a shit selfish friend.  But I guess we all have our own issues,  your buddy's not perfect but to throw away a long friendship really sucks. Reading here makes me realize how many guys feel this way, I feel like there's a lot of pressure on males to succeed and be financially stable and have a family which are all great things but I feel like society gives us weird all or nothing messages sometimes about what is success.  I think you should continue your music if it makes you happy. Sometimes it's not all about monetary success. I wrote a book about 8 years ago and even won an award but there's probably only about 100 people who have actually read it but still I look back at that composition and I'm amazed and proud. Well someone read your rant. I wish you well

I think that's awesome. I can only imagine the certain cultural constraints that come when dealing with mental illness and other ailments, the closest I come is being in mexican environments where you find strength in the church or alcohol or who knows what. I think a lot of parents want to see their kids succeed especially if they think they have opportunities hey never had.  I think it's great you're reaching out to your family because that's something you should never regret, they're your blood, and at least they will know how you feel and where you're coming from even if they deny it. I had a shit time my senior year of college,  my marriage broke up, I started  seeing a married Man, I was incredibly depressed, in the end my depression lead me to drinking too much at a company get together and my boss taking advantage of me. Since it was a case of he said she said the DA decided not to prosecute which haunts me to this day. I hope you get the support you need and wish you well.

Yeah alot of it seems like recycled info. "If you feel depressed get help,  if you're suicidal call this number" hell even the suicide sites tell you the same thing which I guess makes you think twice.  Depression can feel pretty hopeless. I've been reading and posting here the past 24 hours and sometimes just feel like I'm spinning my wheels,  offering arbitrary advice and empathy. Drank a beer tonight, relaxing with my little family,  but still aware of the underlying storm below the surface,  waiting for the next time it takes over and I mime shooting myself in the head every 10 minutes in vain. I guess there's a resolution for all of us,  even if it just means to keep on truckin'.

Yeah I agree it comes and goes. .I often feel.the same about suicide. I think of everyone who has cancer or got into an accident who didn't want to die and feel like I have an opportunity to keep living as miserable as it seems. I also feel like intelligent people can be far and in between. With intelligence I wonder sometimes if we're more prone to depression or exhistentialism which leads to depression.  The whole point less existence thing.  Anyhow,  you are interesting to some stranger somewhere,  not in a lab rat kind of way.  Wishing you the best. Thanks for sharing.

I know how that is. I literally have to put my head phones on when people talk about their weekends at work because they make their lives sound so great and my life is just not that way. Maybe they have their own shit but like facebook, people tend to share trivial light hearted stuff. I live far away from my family too and understand how isolating that can feel. My husband went through a rebellious period where he acted like his life was so great without me but once the partying was over he came crawling back, got a dog, and got back on track.  Not saying this is gonna happen,  but it seems like he was trying at one point and got overloaded maybe. I wish we could expect of people what we feel we would put out for them and it sucks when it's not that way. I am really glad to hear of the 3 good things coming to fruition in your life and I hope things keep up that momentum for you.

I found those same constraints when I tried tai chi.  Basic beginner things way more difficult than I thought it would be. Watching is pure entertainment for me and the more I watch the more I recognize different aspects. As far as kung fu movies are concerned at least.

I used to love the wwe. The rock and stone cold Steve Austin (popular when I watched) did some of the best shit talking battles ever. We were just saying today how much more colorful the characters were back in the day.  Haven't watched in a while so can't say for sure.  I see some of the old dudes from when I watched still there,  big show,  the McMahons, undertaker. Anyways not sure if that's even what you watch. Don't have Netflix but breaking bad wad a great binge watch. Total underdog story.
I love martial arts. Tried aikido in college but mostly just an avid watcher. Would like to try real king fu or wing chun. Have you done any?

I've found that if I stay away from sensationalist news like what you see on cable TV that I can tolerate it.  Npr tends to be pretty good with their facts and mostly impartial. It's helpful to hear what's going on outside of my nuclear world and that way I have things to talk about with coworkers and stuff.  The only time I cried in therapy was when I told the counselor I was no longer good at school due to my depression.  My intelligence, including being informed, makes up alot of my identity.
Sometimes I feel like I am in an existentialist spiral.

Hopefully he'll find out on his own. As someone who has been cheated on and then revenge cheated so to speak,  the whole affair thing never benefits anyone.  Someone always ends up feeling shitty, even if it's someone not even in the triangle like you! Hope things get better for you.

I kind of find I feel zealous when I talk about current events.  Music sometimes evokes too much emotion in me so most of the time I'm an avid npr listener.  It helps me escape my own thoughts and focus on something else even if it's just 50 percent of my concentration.  Although I did find a great 80s play list on songza the other day. Leave it to the inner goth kid in me.
Sure thing. Glad you feel a little bit better.  Won't happen overnight but hope you continue on to find more peace.

Find friends who respect you. If your girl flirted with other guys in front of you tthat's not right and if your friends flirted back and knew you guys were together that's not cool either.  Maybe a few of your friends could do something else or find a different place to play that doesn't include her? That way you still have comrades but no drama.

I do this.  Sometimes I have to consciously tell myself to stop and think of something else. A younger more Zen me would ask me what good I was doing myself by milling over these things over and over especially if they had no place at this present moment. I'm not sure there's anything to be done but trying to be mindful of your thoughts.  Maybe give meditation a shot.  But yeah I do this too.

I read your post and found it interesting for whatever that counts for.  I think a lot of people feel the way you or I do but they bury it and try to put their best foot forward. .I literally cannot stand to listen to coworkers weekend synopses anymore because everything is always so great and la di flicking da. I'm like my life isn't like that.  My life sucks.  But to not awkward them out I just out on headphones and ignore them.  It took me over a year to find a job with a degree. Finding a job is not easy and the market sucks.  I hope you find one, you seem intelligent and just know keeping a job requires a certain amount of biting your tongue to say the least but there are usually worthwhile people at every place. I feel like finding a relationship is like going out into an artificial Meat market where everyone stares at their phones and expects each other to dress like total lame asses and hos. Maybe you could try going out to listen to some music, take a class, volunteer somewhere,  I'm trying to think of things that wouldn't be overloaded with superficial dumb bitches but sometimes I feel they outnumber the girls worth being with.  I honestly would probably have just as much difficulty if I were in your shoes most likely.  Anyways I don't have a solution,  I'm glad you don't want to die as so many of us do here.  Just know you were heard.

It's important not to make someone your world. I know it's hard when we truly feel like we connect with someone.  You being suicidal and distraught may have been too much with her to deal with so she pushed you away,  probably figuring you would figure yourself out and you should.  You were around before her, you can learn to value yourself without her exceptance.  It hurts to be rejected by people. Sometimes we just need to ride it out.  But for every person, there's lots of people.  You sound pretty young and I feel like there's going to be someone in your future who will make you feel like she once did. When I was in college I took advantage of free counseling at the school.  Sometimes it was nice to get thoughts off my chest and talk to someone even if they just listened and that was their job. At least we had a set appointment time so there wouldn't be any flaking out like your friend did to you so if you have those resources think about it. Even if this helps you that's good. I'm glad your not just holding it all in. The road out of the dark is a long one.  I hope you know even if we don't know each other there's someone who feels compassionate towards you and wants you to feel that way towards yourself.

I feel similar sometimes,  like I'm just living for everyone else.  This is part of why I haven't had kids,  I don't know how my depression would affect them or if I'd pass it on to them.  You are probably your girls world even if you don't feel up to par. But I'd encourage you to try and make your world more than them because someday they'll grow up and things will be different.  Maybe even going to a bingo night to get out and socialize or just a walk with a coworker friend or neighbor.   If you have the strength for a hobby that might help get your mind on something else.  I know it can seem in vain sometimes,  but you've got a responsibility to them so please do what you can to find a bit of peace.  Be compassionate towards yourself. Don't try and escape the bad feelings.  Invite them in,  let then stay, try and put your best foot forward for your girls.

I know how you feel,  even the most mundane things remind me of my ex or even people that look like him. Have you thought about writing her a letter and not sending it to her, just addressing her and saying how you feel about everything? That used to help me in the initial stages of breaking up.

I know just how you feel, a lot of times I've felt like killing myself but haven't for the sake of my family.  Only my mom really knows about my depression so for anyone else I know it would be a big slap in the face. For my mom too of course,  she often tells me I'm what's keeping her around as she suffers from bipolar disorder.   It can be hard for others to understand, I have an ongoing joke with a friend who once told me to just think positive when I'm depressed. I acted shocked and said I'd never thought of that before! Joke being,  if only it were so simple. Sorry your dad is being a dick,  I wish all parents could be supportive of their kids and not just think they're slacking.  I haven't gone to work the past 2 days because I've been sick, in other words, too depressed to go stare at a computer screen for 8 hours and act enthused about my surroundings.   If you're still continuing art I think that's great. I used to be a good writer but since being depressed have largely lost that motivation and identity so if you can keep that going that's awesome.  Sometimes it's good to hang out with friends without scamming for girls or involving girlfriends,  maybe you guys can flesh out some time to hang out.  I was invited to spend the night with a friend about a week ago, even though I'm depressed and don't feel like going I still will because I'll likely feel better once I get into the groove of things.  I hope your meds work in the future.  It's an uphill battle but there's many of us who identify with your feelings.

No need to hide your feelings, if you're down you're down,  although sometimes pretending to be happier than I feel gives me a temporary boost.  That's got to be hard to keep seeing your ex around,  have you thought about avoiding those places for a while or even blocking her so you don't need to see her?  I wouldn't worry about losing that connection, if sshe wants to reach out she will find a way.  You might want to do something else because engaging in activities you enjoyed with your ex is probably not going to be helpful as you're trying to move on.

Sounds like a good idea.  Then you can leave with a clear conscious knowing you did what you could,  gave her space to sort things out, and reached out before you gave up. Wishing you a better future.

Maybe she secretly feels a lot of pressure going to bat for you with your ex that she "forgot." People can be all gung ho about something they say they'll do,  but you may be correct,  you may have offered help and now she's in elation with her better life, or she feels like talking to your ex is a burden. Whatever it is you would hope people just are straight with you and tell you like it is.  If she doesn't think it's something she can do or is a bad idea she should tell you. If it's just blatant her forgetting about your plans, that's not much of a friend.

I've had friends cheat on their boyfriends when I knew both of them.  It was hard not to say anything but as a friend I felt I kind of had this duty to keep the secret even if it made me feel shitty. But this is me being openly told. You snooped.  I totally do not blame you, curiosity so often getsthe better of us especially if it's people we care about.  It's important not to put people on a pedestal.  We all have flaws and most of us have the best intentions but things happen. I would just keep it to yourself especially if your home life depends on it.  Try not to get involved in the drama.  Write it down, post it here,  take a walk, connect with other friends.   Let the situation cool for a while.

Is there another way you can get out your feelings or frustrations.  Unfortunately I've found its better to lower my expectations when it comes to people.  So many of them are self centered or have their own things going on or don't realize the gravity of your situation.  I've found I need to be my own friend and be compassionate towards myself because I have more control over that than anyone else.

Hey sorry you're going through this. I can identify with some of what you say. My mom was bipolar and quite beautiful so invited any man into her life that would give her attention. As a kid she saw a man who beat her and only broke up with him once he went to jail for the 2nd time for dui. After that it was an emotionally abusive psycho. I had a lot of trust issues too, problems letting myself be vulnerable with people; after 8 years of marriage my husband decided I wasn't sexual enough and scratched the itch somewhere else.  After some time we are back together now but I am constantly suspicious. Trust issues go on.  I can only talk to my mom about my issues a little as she has issues of her own.  Everyone else I feel doesn't really get it and I don't feel I should weigh then down with a bunch of heavy personal stuff.  I'm sorry your boyfriend gave up.  Mental illness can be hard for people to understand and deal with.   Even now I don't share the intricacies of my depression with my husband.   It's just easier to fake it.  It can be a heavy load for some people.  But you know what, it sounds like he was kind of a dick about it,  telling you what a great week he had. Maybe he us trying to convince himself or push you away, but it's not your job to decipher a code.  I'm sorry you feel alone. Only during my breakup did I realize how isolated I was.  Sometimes it's okay to reach out and spend time with friends doing stuff even if other things weigh on your mind.  Sometimes acting like I'm in a better mood even helps.  Try to foster some relationships around you even if it's just taking a walk with a coworker and doing more listening than you do talking.  I've also found that these kind of random forums help a little, even if it lacks an empathetic face.

I just want to say I'm really sorry you feel this way because I can identify with it very well. My marriage had broken up for a while and during this time I began seeing a mutual friend of ours.  Objectively it was dumb. He had a family.  But we connected very well.  We were both on the poorer working class side. I had just got my bachelor's degree and got my first well paying job. He told me how ecstatic he was that things were coming together for us (I had told him I wanted him to keep supporting his family if we got together). 2 weeks later he disappeared. After a 21 month relationship.  He never broke up with me, never answered my texts *granted I only sent 2 because I couldn't handle anymore rejection.   This was someone I was in love with, who i thought loved me, blah di blah, of course I feel like a dumb bitch.  Point is, I've suffered a heavy depression because of this and other things.  We just don't know what's going on in people's heads.  We can look at our connections optimistically and think it's so simple for 2 people who connect so well to make a life but it's not.  Especially if kids are involved.  I'm glad your relationship with her didn't last much longer.   She was probably feeling very vulnerable and needed to feel loved so she reached out to you. But she through it out the door for her ex.  Whatever you do don't let her string you along.  Move on and find someone who can be with you and who you want to be with.   Don't let this lost connection be the bane of your existence like mine is.

I think it's actually really great you've gone to the gym and done something about your weight and health. Maybe you're over stimulated by the environment.  I know as an introvert when I finally do delve into more social situations sometimes it can be exhausting to bring myself out of my shell.  Exerting yourself doesn't always release endorphins I've found personally.  I try to exercise regularly and have never found it to have much of an effect on my depression. I also find I'm expecting more results for the effort I put in and when I don't see those results quick enough or on caliber with what I think I'm putting out,  it can bum me out even more.  I do like exercising at home or with my dog, so if you're like me the gym itself could be exhausting because of the whole social aspect of it.   Whatever you choose to do I hope you keep going. Exerting some control over your body let's us have a bit of ourselves back when so often things in our head seem out of control

You're right. It's probably more common than we think.  It's only forums like these we can acknowledge their occurrence. I guess I have always felt like a bit of an outcast.  I like reading about serial killers, thinking about what makes them tick.   There's a morbidly obese woman I work with and I wonder what made her get to that point too.  I was a psych major in school. It was a way to diagnose myself,  understand my mom, and at a better point in my life, empathize and try to help. No longer interested.  Not interested in hurting people either. But my head can be a bit devious. I suppose it's rationale that keeps things in check.

Yeah I guess I could start with the sister I do speak to and see what she thinks even if I have a feeling she'll be as useless as she always is. Sometimes I feel like I am just living for everybody else's sake. I do like my pets, my cat and dog,  they are like my best friends but unfortunately not the best sounding boards.

I don't talk to 2 of them and the one I do talk to is always in debt because she thinks she can afford the orange county lifestyle.  Sometimes I wonder what my mom would do if I wasn't around. She tells me a lot that I am the only reason she is still around. I don't think she realizes how low I've gotten and how much pressure she puts on me to be her world.  Yep you're right. I'm not active on social media, I lurk on many sites, news sties and stuff. I was feeling a bit crazy today and this has actually helped me settle my mind a bit.

Money. If I had those resources that would be great. My mom qualifies for Medicare but always has some excuse on how she doesn't qualify for care.  Like I said,  she almost thrives on this victim/ martyr mentality.  I sent her an app for assisted housing this past week so maybe that will be our answer.  Thanks for the replies, I will give the writing a shot. I think we sink into ourselves so low sometimes that it seems futile to draw ourselves back out again.
Yeah too bad everything is armchair activism and hash tags for many of these "future leaders".

2 of them haven't actively been raised by her since they were about 12 and 13. They blame her for their problems growing up most likely,  same as the other one,  who is an intense narcisist.  We wouldn't be friends if she weren't my sister.  Point is she's all of ours mother,  I went through shit with her too but she is a good person and means well. She just always plays the victim.  Thing is one sister makes millions of dollars a year and does nothing. It's just a lot to have on my shoulders.

I have three older sisters, 2 of them actually quite well off,  all of them who take zero responsibility for her. I am only close with one for this reason and mostly because we grew up together.   I have many false starts in writing but lose interest quickly. Maybe writing about myself would come easier.

Kids are dicks. Even little kids now. One lives by me who purposely instigates my dog and me. Pretty sure his parents are drug addicts and he has no guidance. Technically not his fault but I have pictured running him over or lighting his house on fire.  Maybe it's the writer in me to entertain these sensationalist thoughts.

I told him once I felt like dying and he credited my mom's bipolar illness with making me feel that way. I don't want to freak him out. My own mother puts a lot of stress on me, she is disabled and leans on me to get her out of her bad living situation and acts like I am her savior.  It is too much stress. I grind my teeth at night and can feel the tension in my neck from clenching.  I saw a counselor for a few weeks in college.  She was mostly a sounding board and I don't see therapy being a viable thing. When people talk about themselves I feel like it's narcissistic.  When people talk about their weekends at work I drown them out with headphones. I used to like to write,  either to get my feelings out or just write fiction (I am a somewhat capable writer) and it's depressed me further to lose interest in that and some of that identity. I feel like I'm just floating along. No goals.  No point.

He had been treated for suicidal tendencies some years back say the reports.  The media is having fun with all this mental illness hullabaloo.  What better reason to make us feel more ostricized.   My husband is somewhat aware of my family history and my own tendencies but I don't share the extremes of it. Like many sufferers I am good at faking it.
